findings.where: First screen, the hero's ground behind the heading, paragraphs, notes and photograph (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pale gradient that runs from blue to lavender and pink. It is not the warm paper the tile's own palette names ('A warm paper… Three colours, no accent'), and it is not built from the house blue and grey. This is the first thing the founder sees. A pastel gradient makes the first screen look like a tech product's landing page, not a legal journal, and that colour is used nowhere else on the page, so the hero and everything below it look like two different designs.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges the first screen first. He asked for every tile to be built in or around the house colours, and the research asks for a warm paper ground with one ink and at most one accent, avoiding 'slick'. A development-bank visitor would see a generic SaaS gradient, not an advisor's serious page.

findings.where: First screen, the first paragraph 'I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…', set in bold, widely spaced sans capitals (desktop and phone; on phone it runs to eight lines)
findings.fault: The one sentence that says what Mark does and who he does it for is set as four to eight lines of spaced capitals. On the squint it is the second-loudest thing on the page and outweighs his serif paragraph. It reads like a corporate label or a banner, not like Mark speaking. It also adds a third type voice to a hero that already has a large light serif, a regular serif and the sans notes, so the first screen looks busier than a well-set brief.
findings.who_objects: The founder asked for Mark to be heard in the first person and for serious, refined type, with no tracked 'techy' capitals. A bank officer who scans for what he does would find the key sentence the slowest text on the screen to read.

findings.where: Header, the lockup: aqueduct mark and 'MMM INFRA' on the left, 'Mark M. Moseley' to its right (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The firm's mark comes first in reading order and is the larger, darker shape, while Mark's name sits second at a modest size. So in the header the firm leads and the person follows.
findings.who_objects: The founder's personal-advisor test asks for his name to lead, with the logo beside it, because 'the firm is the brand' fails. A visitor's eye lands on the aqueduct and 'MMM INFRA' before it reaches the name.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the margin notes 'Istanbul, 2025', 'Melbourne, 2026' and 'São Paulo, 2024' placed in between the heading, the photograph and the paragraphs, with 'Write to me' at the end
findings.fault: With no margin to sit in, the notes fall into the text column as loose bold-and-small lines between blocks. They read like captions or subheads, not as the place and year of the work beside each paragraph, and each one breaks up the hero's reading. Together with the photograph and the eight-line capitals paragraph they push the one action down to the third phone screen.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone who arrives from LinkedIn has to scroll past three unexplained interruptions before reaching the way to write to Mark, and may not connect the notes with his work at all.

findings.where: First screen, the proof beside the action
findings.fault: Next to 'Write to me', the only evidence of work is three talk titles. No body that asked Mark for advice, no role and no project is named, and 'I advise multilateral development banks…' is a claim that nothing can be checked against. The page holds no third-party proof anywhere.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank and agency staff choose consultants on relevant experience by project type and region. Before writing, they want to see that he has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs. Talks show expertise, but not that clients have hired him.

findings.where: Motion section (desktop): the replay photograph and its table in the right column, the curve on the left
findings.fault: The photograph floats far right and lower than the heading it illustrates, and a large empty block opens under the curve on the left. The section falls apart into two pieces that do not read as one exhibit, and the empty block looks like something failed to load.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the motion sketch has to search for the element the heading talks about, and the empty space makes the tile look unfinished.
